categories.name: Ordinary thick bricks
categories.scope: This class includes ordinary rectangular and round bricks. Slopes go in C. Arches and special connecting pieces go in D.

categories.name: Rectangular bricks
categories.scope: These are ordinary rectangular bricks in the existing records. I use the recorded size to create sub-classes. Stud count alone does not show the shape.

categories.name: Rectangular bricks, 1x2
categories.scope: Ordinary 1x2 bricks without a recorded side stud or pin.

categories.name: Rectangular bricks, 1x4
categories.scope: Ordinary rectangular bricks recorded as 1x4.

categories.name: Rectangular bricks, 2x2
categories.scope: Ordinary rectangular bricks recorded as 2x2. Round bricks go in A2.

categories.name: Rectangular bricks, 2x4
categories.scope: Ordinary rectangular bricks recorded as 2x4.

categories.name: Round bricks
categories.scope: Ordinary cylindrical bricks. TG027 is recorded as 2x2. This does not provide its size in millimetres.

categories.name: Thin pieces: plates and tiles
categories.scope: This class includes ordinary plates and tiles. Bases with a vertical pin go in D2.3. Having no top studs does not by itself make a piece a tile.

categories.name: Plates
categories.scope: Ordinary plates, grouped by their recorded size. Bases with a vertical pin are excluded.

categories.name: Plates, 1x10
categories.scope: Plates recorded as 1x10.

categories.name: Plates, 2x3
categories.scope: Plates recorded as 2x3.

categories.name: Plates, 2x4
categories.scope: Plates recorded as 2x4.

categories.name: Plates, 2x6
categories.scope: Plates recorded as 2x6.

categories.name: Plates, 4x6
categories.scope: Plates recorded as 4x6.

categories.name: Tiles
categories.scope: The current pieces are round eye tiles. Size is not recorded for TG001, TG006 or TG011, so I leave it blank.

categories.name: Slopes
categories.scope: This class includes upright, inverted and curved slopes. TG007 goes in C3, but its different source names still need checking.

categories.name: Regular slopes
categories.scope: Slopes whose recorded names do not include inverted. They are grouped by recorded size.

categories.name: Regular slopes, 1x2
categories.scope: Upright slopes recorded as 1x2.

categories.name: Regular slopes, 1x3
categories.scope: Upright slopes recorded as 1x3.

categories.name: Regular slopes, 2x2
categories.scope: Upright slopes recorded as 2x2.

categories.name: Inverted slopes
categories.scope: The recorded names include inverted slope. Both current pieces are recorded as 1x3.

categories.name: Curved slopes
categories.scope: I place TG007 here after checking its picture. The source names curved brick and arch are retained because their meaning still needs checking.

categories.name: Structural and connection pieces
categories.scope: This proposed class includes arches, special connecting pieces, rods, ladders and rotors. These listed structures take priority over ordinary brick or plate form. D is not a general class for all unusual pieces.

categories.name: Arches
categories.scope: TG009 and TG014 are recorded as Arch. TG007 remains in C3, whilst its source names are kept for checking.

categories.name: Special connection pieces
categories.scope: These pieces have a side stud, horizontal pin or vertical pin. Ordinary top studs alone do not place a piece here.

categories.name: Bricks with a side stud
categories.scope: The recorded names include a side stud. This connecting structure places the pieces here rather than in A.

categories.name: Bricks with a horizontal pin
categories.scope: The recorded name includes a horizontal pin. This connecting structure places the piece here rather than in A.

categories.name: Bases with a vertical pin
categories.scope: TG048 is recorded as a pin base. Its name also includes plate with vertical pin. I give the vertical pin priority and place it here rather than in B.

categories.name: Rods
categories.scope: Pieces recorded as Rod. Their use as an aerial or antenna remains a keyword or model role.

categories.name: Ladders
categories.scope: Pieces recorded as Ladder. The recorded size describes the top connection, not the whole piece.

categories.name: Rotors
categories.scope: The current piece is a four-arm rotor. This classification uses its recorded name and type. Its rotation has not been tested.

categories.name: Minifigure and decorative pieces
categories.scope: This proposed class includes minifigure parts, flags and flowers. Their component identity takes priority over connecting features. Other pieces do not enter E simply because they have a decorative use.

categories.name: Minifigure parts
categories.scope: These are recorded minifigure heads, torso assemblies and legs. Their category is based on component type, not their meaning in a model.

categories.name: Minifigure heads
categories.scope: Pieces recorded as Minifigure part and named head.

categories.name: Minifigure torso assemblies
categories.scope: TG046 includes a torso, white arms and yellow hands. I keep it as one recorded resource rather than giving its parts new identifiers.

categories.name: Minifigure legs
categories.scope: TG022 is recorded as one legs component. I do not divide it into separate resources without separate identifiers.

categories.name: Decorative pieces
categories.scope: This proposal includes flags and flowers here. A decorative use alone does not place another piece in this class.

categories.name: Flags
categories.scope: Pieces recorded as Flag.

categories.name: Flowers
categories.scope: Pieces recorded as Flower. Colour, transparency and stud count remain attributes rather than main class rules.

terms.relationships: Broader term BT: Decorative piece

terms.relationships:

Narrower term NT: Round eye tile
terms.scope: Round tiles. All current examples are further described as Round eye tile.

useEntries.scope: This entry refers to TG009 and TG014. TG007 remains in C3.
Here, Block leads to ordinary Brick. The two words are not treated as equivalent in every context.
This entry refers to the torso assembly TG046. It does not mean a whole minifigure or any object used as a body in a model.
Here, Bow refers to the arches TG009 and TG014, not a weapon, ribbon bow or other meaning of the word.
This entry refers to the whole brick with a horizontal pin, not the pin alone.
This entry refers to the whole brick with a side stud, not the stud alone.
Here, Cylinder refers to the ordinary round brick TG027, not every cylindrical or round piece.
This entry refers to an actual minifigure head, not an ordinary brick used as a head or brain in the model.
This entry refers to the recorded minifigure legs component, not any piece used as legs in a model.
Here, Pin base refers to TG048. This does not mean that every pin base has a vertical pin.
This entry refers to the whole connecting base TG048. It is classified in D rather than as an ordinary plate in B.
Here, Propeller leads to the four-arm rotor TG052. Rotor and Propeller are not treated as equivalent in every mechanical context.
This entry leads to Slope within this local thesaurus. It does not make all roof tiles or all tiles equivalent to slopes.
Here, Streamer refers to the wavy flags TG019 and TG024. It does not mean that all streamers are flags.
This entry refers to an actual minifigure torso component.
